test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

She said that she could bake cookies.

options.text: She had said, “I can bake cookies.”

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that she could bake cookies.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"she could bake" becomes "I can bake"**
 
 
• Pronoun "she" is changed to "I" to match direct speech.
 
• Verb "could" is changed to "can" to match the present tense in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "she said"
 
• Converted to: "she said", maintaining the statement format.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "I" and ends with a period ".".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She said, “I can bake cookies.”"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: She had said, “I can bake cookies.”

 
 
• Changes the reporting verb to past perfect tense, which does not match the original sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "She says, ‘I can bake cookies.’" 
 
 
• Changes the reporting verb to present tense, which does not match the original sentence
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She said, ‘I may bake cookies.’" 
 
 
• Changes the verb from "can" to "may", altering the meaning of the sentence.
